turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come, sit. I will check the pressure before doctor calls you. The token was a bit delayed, sorry.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, it's okay. All this for a small thing only.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He didn't want to come. I had to drag him from the godown gate.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is one thirty eight over eighty four. Pulse seventy six. Saturation 98 percent.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello, I'm doctor Shah. Sit comfortably. What has been bothering you?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Bothering is a big word. Umm, there is a small lump, right side groin. Comes when I lift, goes when I lie down. That's all.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Tell me a bit more, in your own words. When did you first notice it?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, three four months back I think. I didn't mark any date. It is not troubling me much.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He says that, but in the evening he is pressing it and making a face. My sister, she had a groin swelling last year, got operated in her town, so I got scared for him.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): I understand why you worried. Does the lump pain, or is it only the swelling?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Little bit ache only, by evening, after the shift. Morning the lump itself I forget.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): And vomiting? Any of that?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No vomiting. I am eating my rice as usual.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever? Or the skin over it turning red?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Skin is normal, not red. See, nothing.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Also, uh, when I push it with my hand it goes in. Simple.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good that it goes back. Let me examine you. Please stand up and cough.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. There is a soft swelling in the right groin, it bulges when you cough, and it reduces when I press. Left groin is clear. Abdomen is soft, no tenderness.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Told you. Small only.

[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): What I feel is most likely a right inguinal hernia. A little bit of bowel is slipping through a weak spot in the groin muscle. Strain pushes it out, lying down lets it fall back.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): So the intestine is coming out? Sounds dramatic. People in the godown have this and they still load.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): It can stay quiet for a long time, true. The worry is if the bowel gets stuck and the blood supply is cut. That is an emergency, not a small thing.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Then what do we do, doctor? He will not sit at home.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): We will come to the lifting. Before that, any illnesses you already have, any tablets?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Pressure, only mild. I take amlodipin, five milligram, one in the morning. Nothing else.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright, blood pressure is ongoing, amlodipine five mg every morning. Family side, anyone with sugar, heart problems, pressure?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not have sugar or any such thing, my elder brother had a heart attack around sixty, and another sister has pressure but no sugar.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): And day to day, the work, food, exercise, any alcohol?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I am a loader at the godown near the highway, twelve hour shifts, six days a week. Food is rice and dal, whatever the canteen puts, and I don't do exercise separately, the loading is the exercise. Whisky, one peg, two times in a week, not more than that.

[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): That is heavy work for this. Please don't lift the full sacks for now. If something light has to be moved, bend the knees, hold it close, and don't strain while holding the breath.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, if I tell the supervisor no lifting, he will put someone else on my spot. The lump is tiny.

[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): I hear the job worry, truly. A stuck hernia will take you off work for longer than lighter duty will. I am sending you to the general surgeon, we will book that from this clinic.

[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): I will enter the surgical referral before you go. My own child had a small procedure last month, the surgery waiting room fills by nine, so reach a little early when they give the date.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Early, late, all this running around. Fine, we will go.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the lump will not go back in, or the pain becomes severe, or you start vomiting, come to emergency the same day.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya ya. If it sticks I will come. Otherwise no drama.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): And come back to see me in six weeks, once the surgeon has seen you, so we know how the lifting is going.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will make sure he comes. Left to him he will say next month next month.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): The amlodipine, are you actually taking it every morning?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Most mornings. Umm, the shift is from five sometimes, I forget. Maybe two times in a week I miss.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Try not to miss it, especially if an operation comes up. Keep the strip near the bed so the early shift doesn't steal it.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Hmm. Okay, I will keep it there.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): I have noted one thirty eight over eighty four and pulse seventy six on the paper for the surgeon.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Those are fine for today. Any other question in your mind?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): You are not giving any tablet for the lump, no?
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): No new tablet for the lump from my side. The surgeon will talk about repair. The ache you can watch, it is mild.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. Less tablets the better. The bus was packed today, anyway.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Thank you doctor. We will do the early morning thing and the no heavy sack thing.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take care, both of you. Go slow with the sacks till the surgeon says otherwise.

spec.situation: Manual worker with a groin lump that appears on lifting and goes away lying down; mild ache by evening; no vomiting; surgical referral planned, advice on lifting.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Medication, dose, indication stated; 'currently_used' is incomplete because he misses about two doses weekly.
bad.text: amlodipin (generic_name=amlodipine, dose=5 mg, frequency=once daily in the morning, indication=hypertension, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient stated the groin lump can be manually pushed back in ('when I push it with my hand it goes in').
Examination finding omitted: the right groin swelling bulges on coughing.
Family history detail omitted: mother did not have diabetes or similar illness.

Surgical referral logistics/plan omitted: nurse will enter the surgical referral before the patient leaves, and advised reaching the surgery clinic early because the waiting room fills by nine when the date is given.
Planned follow-up context omitted: return in six weeks once the surgeon has seen him so they can review how the lifting/work restrictions are going.
No medication was prescribed for the hernia/lump; doctor explicitly said no new tablet for the lump and that the surgeon will discuss repair.
